title: RBAC v2 evidence automation roadmap (Q2 2026) notes
body:
Purpose:
Quick working notes for automating evidence collection for RBAC v2, shaping the SIEM export schema, and operationalizing quarterly least-privilege recertification. Rough roadmap for Q2 2026 with checklists, sample queries, and open questions.

Context / constraints:
- RBAC v2 rollout planned across hosted/dedicated/private by end of Q2.
- Current audit logs are semi-structured; we need a canonical export for SIEM and for the recertification evidence store.
- Goal is to reduce manual reviewer work during quarterly access reviews by >= 60% via automated evidence (last access, purpose tags, justification history, approvals).
- Privacy: we cannot export customer PII. Exported event schema must be redacted or flagged.

High-level goals (Q2):
1) Define an exportable audit schema that covers role assignments, overrides, delegation, and temporal grants.
2) Implement a lightweight evidence aggregator that synthesizes: role catalog, assignment history, last-use telemetry, approval artifacts.
3) Wire outputs to SIEM (Graylog -> Splunk -> SIEM ingest) and to the recertification UI as pre-filled review packets.
4) Ship an initial automation flow for 2 pilot teams (SRE + Solutions Eng) to validate review heuristics.

Proposed components:
- RBAC event producer (serving-runtime + console) emits normalized events to kafka-topic: rbac-v2-audit.v1
- Enrichment service (python lambda) consumes events, joins with identity metadata (SCIM/OKTA snapshot) and telemetry (API access logs), writes canonical records to evidence-store (S3 partitioned by quarter) and to SIEM forwarder (jsonlines).
- Evidence-store UI integration: precompute review-packets (per-user / per-role) and expose via console -> Security > Access Reviews -> "Pending Automation".
- Scheduler (Airflow) kicks off quarterly pipeline: snapshot assignments, diff to previous quarter, create review tasks, send Slack reminders and export to SIEM for long-term retention.

Draft audit export schema (canonical fields) - this is initial, need feedback from infra and SRE:
- event_id: uuid
- event_type: role_assignment | role_revocation | role_change | override_grant | delegation | role_definition_change
- actor_id: user_id (redacted=false/true)
- actor_display: short name/email (redact flag applied downstream)
- target_id: user_or_service_id
- target_type: user | service_account | machine
- role_id: builtin/tenant:role-name
- role_version: semver or timestamp
- grant_scope: global | project:proj-id | org:org-id
- grant_start: iso8601
- grant_end: iso8601 or null
- justification_id: uuid (links to approval artifact)
- approval_flow: manual | workflow-id | emergency-bypass
- origin: console | api | provisioning | api-key | terraform
- last_used: iso8601 (best-effort, computed by enrichment)
- use_count_90d: integer
- evidence_bucket_path: s3://evidence/.../q?=2026-Q2
- siem_index: string
- redaction_level: none | partial | full
- raw_payload_ref: db_ref (pointer into blob store, access-controlled)

Note: SIEM output should include a small "recertification_score" heuristic (0-100) to help prioritize manual review (see heuristics below).

Recertification heuristic (first pass):
- recert_score = weighted( last_used (40%), use_count_90d (25%), time_since_grant (15%), explicit_justification_recent (10%), emergency_bypass (negate 50%) )
- Scores under 30 => auto-revoke candidate or require expedited review.

Sample SQL (platform warehouse) to get current active role assignments (for enrichment):
-- current assignments as of snapshot_date
SELECT a.user_id, a.role_id, a.grant_start, a.grant_end, r.role_tier, i.last_login
FROM rbac_assignments a
JOIN rbac_roles r ON a.role_id = r.id
LEFT JOIN identity_last_login i ON i.user_id = a.user_id
WHERE (a.grant_end IS NULL OR a.grant_end > '2026-03-01')
AND a.revoked = FALSE;

Sample query for last use (tokenized logs -> materialized view):
SELECT user_id, role_id, max(event_time) as last_used, count(*) filter (where event_time > now() - interval '90 days') as use_count_90d
FROM api_activity_logs
WHERE attributed_role IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY user_id, role_id;

Runbook sketch: Quarterly recertification pipeline (automated-first):
1) 00:00 day 1 of quarter: Airflow triggers "snapshot-assignments" -> writes to evidence-store with partition Qn.
2) Enrichment job joins telemetry and identity data; computes recert_score; persists prefill-packets.
3) Create review tasks in review-queue (Console) for owners: role_owners + downstream_app_owners.
4) Automated decisions: if recert_score >= 80 and last_used within 30 days -> auto-approve. If recert_score <= 20 and use_count_90d == 0 -> auto-suggest-revoke with justification template.
5) Week 1-2: human reviewers triage tickets; automation posts reminders to Slack and emails.
6) Any change (revoke/approve) writes back an audited event with justification id and reviewer id.

Checklist for pilot implementation:
- [ ] Confirm kafka topic naming and retention policy (infra)
- [ ] Schema finalize and JSON Schema file in repo (security)
- [ ] Mapping table for role_id -> owner (product) and for role_tier (SRE)
- [ ] Build enrichment lambda and test with 30-day window (eng-ops)
- [ ] Wire SIEM forwarder; ensure event dedup keys (siem)
- [ ] Privacy review for exported fields (legal)
- [ ] Console UX wires for "prefill review packet" (product-console)
- [ ] Slack notification design + unsubscribe flow (comms)

Failure modes and mitigations:
- Missing telemetry for service accounts -> mark recert_score as unknown and route to manual queue.
- Duplicate events from retries -> dedupe in forwarder using event_id and event_time.
- Large evidence blobs -> store raw_payload_ref in cold storage and keep summaries in SIEM.
- False auto-revoke -> require human sign-off for any revoke that affects enterprise customers until after pilot.

Edge cases:
- Delegations: temporary role delegation should have explicit delegation chain in the schema.
- Cross-tenant service accounts: we must not export tenant identifiers unless allowed for SIEM long-term retention. Consider scrubbing tenant ids and storing mapping in internal-only store.
- Emergency bypasses: these should be flagged and always routed to manual review regardless of score.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we allow SIEM to retain raw_payload_ref? (Legal/Privacy)
- How do we handle third-party identity providers (Okta SCIM v2) and mapping of external group ids?
- Can product own role -> owner mapping or should it be centralized in security?
- Timeline for internal rollout: pilot->2 teams (6 weeks), iterate->company-wide (4 months)

Action items (owners):
- Maya: draft JSON Schema and push to repo (due 2026-03-12)
- Liam: confirm kafka retention & topic creation (due 2026-03-08)
- Anika: build first enrichment lambda prototype and test with synthetic logs (due 2026-03-22)
- Diego: SIEM forwarder config + dedupe policy (due 2026-03-18)
- Priya: privacy checklist and legal sign-off draft (due 2026-03-15)

Notes to self / brainstorm fragments:
- Could compute "purpose inference" from recent ticket titles (linear/jira) if user links are present -> useful to justify access during recertification.
- Consider adding a short-lived "justification_granularity" flag to mark whether justification is team-level vs ticket-level.
- If we add recert_score to SIEM, ensure it's marked as derived and explain calculation to auditors.
- Think about retention: evidence-store raw blobs = 3 years, SIEM index = 1 year (configurable).

Slack-style quick logs (temp):
- @diego: siem forwarder needs dedupe key; propose event_id + role_version
- @anika: enrichment lambda will batch on partition_date to avoid hot reads
- @maya: product-owned mapping ok for pilot, security should own global mapping later

End of notes. This doc is intentionally rough; will convert to a formal playbook once pilot signals are green.
